html:
Ahtna Nenn' is the land of the Ahtna, an Athabaskan people of the Copper River basin in south-central Alaska. They speak a language of the Athabaskan family.

They lived by salmon fishing on the Copper River, using fish wheels in later times, and by hunting caribou, moose and sheep. The river is named for the native copper they worked and traded, which reached the coast through the Eyak and Tlingit. The Ahtna kept outsiders out for a long time: Russian traders of Russian America who came up the river in the 1790s and 1840s were turned back or killed. An American army expedition crossed their land in 1885. Under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act of 1971 they formed Ahtna, Incorporated. Their neighbours include the Dena'ina.
